terms.grammar: adverb; also written as two words, aliquam diū
evidence: Cic. Clu. 25: aliquam diū incolumem fuisse (Lewis & Short s.v. aliquis)
Cic. Ac. 1.12: Aristum Athēnīs audīvit aliquam diū (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: “awhile, for a while, for some time; also for some considerable time”, most frequent in the historians.

phrases.latin: Postillāc in nostrā piscīnā novā aliquamdiū natō.
phrases.english: After that I swim in our new pool for a while.

sources: Lewis & Short: aliquis · Lewis & Short: diu
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): p. 42.
